01_fluent_unjustified.txt.span: The sodium-potassium pump maintains different sodium and potassium concentrations across the cell membrane.
It moves three sodium ions out of the cell and two potassium ions into the cell.
It uses ATP and changes shape during the transport cycle.
The resulting gradients support the resting membrane potential and electrical signaling.

02_reversed_stoich.txt.span: The pump moves three potassium ions into the cell and two sodium ions out during each cycle.
more positive potassium charge enters than sodium charge leaves

03_passive_conflation.txt.span: Sodium and potassium diffuse through the pump down their concentration gradients.
ATP is present in the cell but is not necessary for this movement.

04_hedged.txt.span: The pump usually moves sodium outward and tends to bring potassium inward.
It might use ATP to change shape
These gradients may sometimes contribute to the membrane potential.

05_offtopic.txt.span: Cells have many important structures that work together.
Mitochondria make energy for the cell
ribosomes build proteins from amino acids
The nucleus stores genetic information and controls many activities.

06_correct.txt.span: The pump exports three sodium ions and imports two potassium ions per cycle.
This creates a small electrical imbalance
Potassium binding and phosphate release then return the pump to its original shape

07_mixed_missing_mechanism.txt.span: The pump sends three sodium ions outside and brings two potassium ions inside.
The ion gradients are important for neurons
I have not explained how the pump changes shape.

08_mixed_wrong_direction.txt.span: ATP adds a phosphate group to the pump
Sodium is then released inside the cell.
phosphate release returns the pump to its first shape.

09_mixed_partial.txt.span: The pump maintains sodium and potassium gradients by moving ions across the membrane.
ATP matters because phosphorylation changes the protein's shape.
the exact numbers of ions moved are not stated here.

10_mixed_justification.txt.span: The pump moves three sodium ions out and two potassium ions in.
The cycle makes the inside slightly negative
potassium is released before phosphate leaves.
